recipe.title: Poulet à la sauce d'arachide et tomates
recipe.description: Morceaux de cuisses de poulet mijotés dans une sauce onctueuse à la pâte d'arachide, relevés de tomates fraîches, citron et piment. Servi avec du riz parfumé.
instructions: Émince l'1 oignon et hache les 2 gousses d'ail.
Coupe les 3 tomates en dés.
Dans une grande casserole, fais chauffer 2 c. à soupe d'huile végétale à feu moyen.
Ajoute les cuisses de poulet (4 pièces) et fais-les dorer 5 minutes de chaque côté, jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient bien colorées.
Retire le poulet et réserve‑le sur une assiette.
Dans la même casserole, ajoute l'oignon émincé et fais‑le suer 3 minutes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne translucide.
Incorpore l'ail et le piment haché, fais revenir 1 minute en remuant.
Ajoute les dés de tomates, puis 120 g de pâte d'arachide. Mélange bien pour obtenir une sauce homogène.
Verse 300 ml d'eau, sale 1 pincée et poivre 1 pincée. Porte à ébullition, puis réduis le feu à doux.
Remets les cuisses de poulet dans la casserole, couvre et laisse mijoter 25 minutes, jusqu'à ce que la viande atteigne 74 °C (jus clair) et se détache facilement.
Presse le jus d'1 citron dans la sauce, mélange une dernière fois.
Pendant ce temps, rince le riz (250 g) et fais‑le cuire dans 500 ml d'eau bouillante salée à feu moyen pendant 12 minutes, jusqu'à absorption complète.
Sers le poulet nappé de sauce d'arachide avec le riz chaud.
tips: Pour une sauce plus lisse, utilise un mixeur plongeant avant d'ajouter le poulet.
Conserve les restes au réfrigérateur 2 jours, réchauffe doucement à feu doux.

recipe.title: Tajine de carottes aux pois chiches
recipe.description: Tajine végétarien aux carottes fondantes et pois chiches parfumés aux épices du Maghreb, servi avec du couscous léger.
instructions: Émince l'1 oignon et hache finement les 2 gousses d'ail.
Dans une grande poêle ou un tajine, fais chauffer 2 c. à soupe d'huile d'olive à feu moyen.
Ajoute l'oignon et fais-le dorer 5 minutes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne translucide.

Incorpore l'ail, 1 c. à café de cumin, 1 c. à café de coriandre, 1/2 c. à café de curcuma et 1 c. à café de ras el hanout, puis fais revenir 1 minute en remuant, jusqu'à ce que les épices dégagent leurs arômes.
Ajoute les 500 g de carottes coupées en rondelles épaisses, mélange bien pour les enrober d'épices.
Verse 250 ml d'eau, porte à ébullition, puis réduis le feu à doux et couvre.
Laisse mijoter 15 minutes, jusqu'à ce que les carottes soient tendres mais encore légèrement croquantes.
Égoutte les pois chiches (boîte), rince-les, puis ajoute‑les dans le tajine.
Assaisonne avec 1 pincée de sel et 1 pincée de poivre, puis laisse cuire encore 5 minutes pour que les pois chiches se réchauffent.
Pendant ce temps, place le couscous dans un bol, ajoute 200 ml d'eau bouillante, couvre et laisse gonfler 5 minutes, puis égrène à la fourchette.
Saupoudre le tajine de 2 c. à soupe de coriandre fraîche hachée avant de servir.
Serre le tajine chaud sur un lit de couscous.
tips: Pour plus de profondeur, ajoute un petit morceau de citron confit haché avec les épices.
Si tu n'as pas de ras el hanout, un mélange de cumin, coriandre, paprika et une touche de cannelle fonctionne bien.

recipe.title: Garlic Ginger Chicken Thighs with Steamed Broccoli and Soy‑Glazed Rice
recipe.description: Tender chicken thighs braised in a fragrant garlic‑ginger soy sauce, served with lightly steamed broccoli and fluffy soy‑glazed rice.
instructions: Rinse 200 g of rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
Combine the rice and 400 ml of water in a saucepan, bring to a boil over medium heat, then cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
While the rice cooks, pat the chicken thighs dry and cut each thigh into bite‑size pieces.
Finely mince 2 garlic cloves and grate 1 tbsp of ginger.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat, add a splash of oil, then add the chicken pieces. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until lightly browned.
Add the minced garlic and ginger, stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in 3 tbsp soy sauce, stir, and let the mixture simmer for 8 minutes, turning the chicken pieces, until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (juices run clear).
Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, then stir in 2 tbsp sliced spring onions.
Meanwhile, cut the broccoli into florets and steam them over boiling water for 4‑5 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Fluff the cooked rice with a fork, drizzle a little extra soy sauce if desired, and serve the chicken alongside the broccoli and rice.
tips: If you prefer a slightly sweeter glaze, add a teaspoon of honey or brown sugar to the soy sauce mixture.
Use the same skillet to deglaze with a splash of water before adding the rice for extra flavor.

recipe.title: Thai‑Style Chicken Fried Rice with Broccoli and Egg
recipe.description: Quick one‑pan fried rice using leftover rice, chicken, broccoli, and a golden scrambled egg, flavored with soy sauce, ginger, and garlic.
instructions: If the rice is not already cooked, rinse 300 g of rice, combine with 600 ml water in a pot, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 15 minutes. Spread the cooked rice on a tray to cool and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes (or use leftover rice).
Trim the broccoli into small florets and blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Cut the chicken thighs into thin strips.
Finely mince 2 garlic cloves and grate 1 tsp ginger.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over medium‑high heat. Add the chicken strips and stir‑fry for 4 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (juices run clear, no pink).
Push the chicken to one side of the wok, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, then crack the 2 eggs directly into the pan. Scramble quickly until just set (no runny liquid), then mix with the chicken.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, and blanched broccoli, stir‑fry for 1 minute.
Stir in the cooled rice, breaking up any clumps, and drizzle 2 tbsp soy sauce over the mixture.
Continue to stir‑fry for 3‑4 minutes, until the rice is heated through and slightly crisp on the edges. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Finish by sprinkling 2 tbsp sliced spring onions and serve immediately.
tips: Cold rice prevents the grains from sticking together and gives the fried rice a better texture.
For extra umami, add a splash of fish sauce or a pinch of toasted sesame seeds.

recipe.description: A light, comforting soup perfect for dinner, featuring silky egg ribbons, tender shredded chicken, and broccoli in a savory soy‑ginger broth.

Season with a pinch of white pepper, then turn off the heat.
Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with 2 tbsp sliced spring onions.

recipe.description: Tacos crujientes rellenos de frijoles negros, aguacate cremoso, tomate fresco y queso, con un toque de lima.

recipe.description: Arroz blanco suelto mezclado con maíz dulce y huevo frito, aromatizado con cebolla y lima, perfecto para un almuerzo rápido.

Cuando el arroz esté listo, incorpora el maíz escurrido y mezcla suavemente 2 minutos para que se caliente.
Exprime el jugo de 1/2 lima sobre el arroz y maíz, y mezcla.
Sirve el arroz con maíz en platos, coloca un huevo frito encima de cada porción y espolvorea 30 g de queso fresco desmenuzado.

recipe.title: Stuffed Aubergine with Chickpea‑Quinoa Pilaf
recipe.description: Tender aubergine halves filled with a hearty chickpea‑quinoa mixture, flavored with lemon, tomato and fresh spinach.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Slice each aubergine lengthwise and scoop out a thin layer of flesh to create a shallow boat; set the scooped flesh aside.

Rinse the quinoa under cold water, then combine 150 g quinoa with 300 ml water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 12 minutes, until water is absorbed and grains are fluffy.

Add the reserved aubergine flesh (roughly chopped), the 200 g chickpeas (drained if canned), and the diced tomatoes; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften.
Stir in the fresh spinach and cook for another 2 minutes, until wilted.
Mix the cooked quinoa into the skillet, squeeze the juice of the lemon, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon the quinoa‑chickpea mixture into the roasted aubergine boats.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tbsp tahini with a splash of warm water (about 1 tbsp) and a pinch of salt to make a drizzle.
Drizzle the tahini sauce over the stuffed aubergines and serve warm.

recipe.title: Spicy Black‑Eyed Bean Stew with Tomato‑Onion Relish
recipe.description: Hearty, protein‑rich stew made from black‑eyed beans, bright tomato‑onion relish and served with fresh bread.
instructions: Rinse the 400 g black‑eyed beans in a colander and place them in a large bowl; cover with plenty of water and soak overnight (at least 8 hours).
Drain the soaked beans and transfer them to a pot; add 800 ml fresh water.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 45 minutes, until the beans are tender but still hold their shape.
While the beans simmer, dice the tomato and finely chop the remaining 1/2 onion.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat; add the chopped onion and sauté for 3 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the diced tomato, 1/2 tsp paprika, a pinch of salt and a pinch of black pepper; cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until the tomato breaks down and the mixture becomes a thick relish.
When the beans are done, drain any excess water, return the beans to the pot, and stir in the tomato‑onion relish.
Simmer together for 2 minutes on low heat, just to blend flavors; adjust seasoning if needed.
Toast the 2 slices of bread, slice into strips, and serve alongside the stew.
tips: If you have a pressure cooker, the beans can be cooked in about 8 minutes after soaking, saving time.
A splash of lemon juice added at the end brightens the stew.

recipe.description: Une soupe réconfortante inspirée des bouillons clairs du Sud‑Est asiatique, idéale pour un dîner léger.

recipe.title: Riz basmati frit à la thaïlandaise avec tofu et chou chinois
recipe.description: Un riz sauté parfumé au citron vert et à la sauce soja, rappelant le « khao pad », idéal pour un dîner rapide et digeste.
instructions: Rince le riz basmati à l’eau froide, puis fais-le cuire dans une casserole avec 400 ml d’eau à feu moyen. Une fois l’ébullition atteinte, couvre, baisse le feu à doux et laisse cuire 12 minutes, jusqu’à absorption complète. Étale le riz sur un plat et laisse refroidir 5 minutes.
Émiette le tofu ferme en petits morceaux.
Coupe le chou chinois en fines lanières et hache la ciboule en rondelles.
Émince les 2 gousses d’ail.

Incorpore le riz refroidi, la sauce soja, le jus de citron vert, le sel et le poivre. Fais sauter 3 minutes en remuant constamment, jusqu’à ce que le riz soit bien chaud et légèrement doré.

recipe.description: Un tagine exprés de cordero picado, garbanzos y verduras, servido sobre el couscous sobrante, para una cena ligera y llena de sabor magrebí.
instructions: Calienta una cazuela a fuego medio y añade 2 cda de aceite de oliva.
Agrega la cebolla picada y sofríe 5 min, hasta que esté translúcida.
Incide la zanahoria en rodajas finas y el pimiento rojo en tiras; añádelos y cocina 4 min más.
Incorpora el cordero picado, sazona con 1 cda de comino, 1 cda de pimentón, 1 cda de ras el hanout, sal y pimienta; cocina 6 min, removiendo, hasta que el cordero pierda el color rosado.
Comprueba la temperatura interna del cordero con un termómetro; debe alcanzar 71 °C (más rosado en el centro) antes de continuar.
Escurre los garbanzos enlatados y añádelos a la cazuela; mezcla y cocina 3 min.
Vierte 200 ml de agua, lleva a ebullición, reduce a fuego bajo y tapa; cocina 15 min, hasta que la zanahoria esté tierna y los jugos se espesen ligeramente.

Mientras tanto, reparte las 2 raciones de couscous en un bol, añade 1 cda de aceite y 2 cda de agua caliente, mezcla y caliéntalo en el microondas 1 min o en una sartén a fuego bajo hasta que esté humeante (solo una vez).
Sirve el tagine sobre una cama de couscous caliente, decorando con cilantro fresco si lo deseas.
tips: Si el tagine queda muy seco, añade un chorrito más de agua al final.
Puedes añadir unas aceitunas verdes picadas para un toque extra.

recipe.title: Pork Tenderloin with Dijon Cream Sauce and Sautéed Leeks
recipe.description: Tender pork medallions cooked quickly and finished in a silky Dijon‑cream sauce, served over caramelised leeks for a light yet satisfying dinner.
instructions: Slice the pork tenderloin into 1‑inch thick medallions; season both sides with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Trim the leeks, slice them into ½‑inch rounds, and rinse to remove any grit.
Peel and finely mince the 3 shallots.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the pork medallions and sear 3 minutes per side, until browned and the internal temperature reaches 63 °C; the meat should be just pink inside. Transfer pork to a plate and keep warm.
In the same skillet, add 1 tbsp butter and the minced shallots. Cook 2 minutes over medium heat, stirring, until softened and fragrant.
Add the leeks to the pan, spread them out, and cook 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until they turn golden and start to caramelise.

Stir in the Dijon mustard, then pour the cream, scraping any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook 4 minutes, until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Return the pork medallions to the skillet, nestle them among the leeks, and heat 2 minutes more, just to re‑warm the meat.
Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt and pepper if needed. Serve immediately, spooning extra sauce over each portion.
tips: Pat the pork dry before searing to achieve a better crust.
If you prefer a richer sauce, increase the cream to 200 ml.
A splash of white wine (30 ml) can be added after the shallots for extra depth.

recipe.title: Green Bean and Leek Sauté with Shallot‑Vinegar Glaze
recipe.description: Crisp green beans and sweet leeks tossed together and finished with a bright shallot‑vinegar glaze, perfect as a light side or a vegetarian main.
instructions: Trim the ends of the green beans and cut any long ones in half so all pieces are roughly 5 cm long.
Rinse the leeks, cut off the dark green tops, slice the white and light‑green parts into ¼‑inch half‑moons.
Peel the 2 shallots and mince them very finely.

Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add the green beans and blanch for 3 minutes, until bright green but still crisp. Drain and immediately transfer to a bowl of ice water to stop cooking; drain again.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the leeks and sauté 5 minutes, stirring, until they soften and develop a light caramel colour.
Add the minced shallots and cook 1 minute more, until fragrant.
Add the blanched green beans, toss to combine, and sauté 4 minutes over medium heat, letting the beans develop a few golden spots.
Stir in the white wine vinegar, and cook 1 minute, allowing the liquid to reduce and coat the vegetables, creating a glossy glaze.
Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, give a final toss, and serve hot.
tips: Do not over‑cook the beans; they should retain a slight crunch for the best texture.
For extra depth, add a splash (½ tbsp) of low‑sodium soy sauce to the glaze.

recipe.title: Gruyère‑Shallot Soufflé with a Hint of Mustard
recipe.description: A light, airy soufflé that showcases the nutty flavour of Gruyère and the sweet bite of shallots, subtly brightened with Dijon mustard – an elegant finish to the meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Butter four 6‑oz ramekins and dust each with a little flour, tapping out the excess.
Finely dice the 2 shallots.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt 1 tbsp butter. Add the shallots and sauté 3 minutes, until translucent.
Stir in 1 tbsp flour and cook 1 minute, forming a light roux.
Gradually whisk in the milk, then the cream, cooking 3 minutes while stirring, until the mixture thickens into a smooth béchamel.

Remove the pan from the heat, add the grated Gruyère and 1 tsp Dijon mustard, stirring until the cheese melts completely. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Let the mixture cool slightly (about 2 minutes).
Separate the eggs: place the whites in a large mixing bowl and the yolks in a small bowl.
Whisk the egg yolks into the cheese‑cream mixture until fully incorporated.
Using clean beaters, whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form (about 3 minutes).
Gently fold one third of the beaten whites into the cheese mixture to lighten it, then carefully fold in the remaining whites in two motions, preserving as much air as possible.
Divide the batter evenly among the prepared ramekins, smoothing the tops with a spatula.
Place the ramekins on a baking sheet and bake 25‑30 minutes, until the soufflés have risen, turned golden, and a thin crust forms. Do not open the oven door during the first 20 minutes.
Serve immediately; the soufflés will begin to deflate after a few minutes.
tips: Make sure no yolk gets into the whites, otherwise they will not whip properly.
For a subtle herb note, add a pinch of dried thyme to the béchamel before adding cheese.
